The MINERvA experiment measured the charged current differential cross section for antineutrino interactions producing two or more neutrons on hydrocarbon at 6 GeV average antineutrino energy.
Neutron production biases energy reconstruction in neutrino oscillation experiments and has been rarely studied with cross section measurements.
The analysis focuses on events with visible hadronic energy (available energy) less than 100 MeV to select 2p2h interactions.
Neutron candidates are identified by isolated charge deposits in the scintillator detector, excluding activity near the interaction vertex and muon track.
The neutron detection efficiency reaches nearly 50% for neutrons with kinetic energy between 10 and 50 MeV.
The MINERvA detector uses a fine-grained scintillator tracker segmented into planes with three orientations and is located upstream of the MINOS near detector.
Simulations use GENIE 2.12.6 with the Valencia 2p2h model, Llewellyn Smith CCQE model, Rein-Seghal resonance model, and Bodek-Yang DIS model, with an empirical tune MnvTunev1.
Final state interactions (FSI) are simulated using GENIE's hA model, an effective single-step algorithm.
The neutron inelastic cross section in GEANT4 was reweighted to match recent neutron interaction data.
The analysis uses a neutron candidate energy deposit threshold of 1.5 MeV and requires neutron candidates to be within 1.5 m of the interaction vertex.
Selected events require muons with momentum between 2 and 20 GeV/c and angles less than 20 degrees relative to the beam direction.
The selected sample contains 299,182 interactions with an estimated 39% efficiency and 39% purity.
Backgrounds include single-neutron final states (mostly CCQE) and events with mis-reconstructed available energy, often involving pions.
Data show fewer low-energy neutron candidates (<10 MeV deposit) than predicted by simulation, consistent with previous MINERvA low-energy results.
Cross section is extracted as a function of muon transverse momentum, which correlates with four-momentum transfer and reduces dependence on neutron modeling.
Allowing events with more than two neutrons reduces dependence on neutron production and interaction modeling.
The measurement disagrees with several leading neutrino interaction models, indicating deficiencies in neutron production modeling.
Neutron modeling techniques from nuclear physics are used to quantify uncertainties in neutron detection.
The study provides constraints useful for oscillation experiments like NOvA, DUNE, and T2K, which rely on accurate neutron modeling.
The MINERvA 6 GeV data reproduce similar neutron modeling discrepancies previously observed at 3 GeV.
The analysis uses sidebands to constrain backgrounds and reduce model dependence in the cross section extraction.
